questions.q: In hypertensive retinopathy, the book lists the phases in which order?
opts: Vasoconstriction phase, then sclerotic phase (atherosclerosis), then exudative phase
Sclerotic phase (atherosclerosis), then vasoconstriction phase, then exudative phase
Vasoconstriction phase, then exudative phase, then sclerotic phase (atherosclerosis)
Exudative phase, then sclerotic phase (atherosclerosis), then vasoconstriction phase
questions.exp: Hypertensive retinopathy runs Vasoconstriction phase -> Sclerotic phase (Atherosclerosis) -> Exudative phase. (Book p164)

questions.q: Keith-Wagner grade 1 shows arteriolar attenuation, with an A:V (diameter) ratio of ___ (normal ___).
questions.exp: Grade 1: arteriolar attenuation; A:V (diameter) ratio = 1:3, whereas normal is 2:3. (Book p164)

questions.q: Match each sign of the Keith-Wagner table with its meaning — 1) Salus sign  2) Bonnet sign  3) Gunn sign  … A) Tapering of blood vessel  B) Deflection of blood vessel  C) Banking of blood vessel
questions.exp: Salus sign = deflection of blood vessel (grade 2); Bonnet sign = banking of blood vessel and Gunn sign = tapering of blood vessel (both grade 3). (Book p164)

questions.q: A fundus examination in a hypertensive patient shows flame shaped hemorrhages together with cotton wool spots. Which Keith-Wagner grade does the book assign to this finding?
questions.exp: Grade 3 in the Keith-Wagner table: Bonnet sign, Gunn sign and flame shaped hemorrhages with cotton wool spots. (Book p164)

questions.q: The bracket drawn beside grades 2 and 3 of the Keith-Wagner table states that the Salus, Bonnet and Gunn signs are seen:
opts: At the optic disc margin in arterioles
Only in the peripheral retina in arteries
questions.exp: The bracket beside grades 2 and 3 reads 'At AV crossings in veins'. (Book p164)

questions.q: Per the Keith-Wagner table, all of the following belong to grade 4 EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Grade 4: copper wiring of arterioles, silver wiring of arterioles and papilledema. Salus sign belongs to grade 2. (Book p164)

questions.q: In the 'Grade 4 HTN retinopathy' photograph, match arrow 1, 2 and 3 with the book's labels — A) Swelling of optic disc  B) Exudates: macular star appearance  C) Cotton wool spots
questions.exp: Labels: 1 Cotton wool spots, 2 Swelling of optic disc, 3 Exudates: macular star appearance: malignant HTN. (Book p164)

questions.q: True or false — 'In the grade 4 photograph, the exudates forming a macular star appearance indicate benign hypertension.' Choose the correct verdict:
opts: False - the book links the macular star exudates to malignant HTN
True - macular star exudates mark benign hypertension
False - the macular star is a sign of cotton wool spots alone
True - the macular star is the sign of papilledema alone
questions.exp: Label 3 in the grade 4 figure: Exudates: macular star appearance: malignant HTN. (Book p164)

questions.q: The 'Grade 3 Hypertensive retinopathy' photograph is annotated with which set of labels?
opts: Cotton wool spots, AV change and hemorrhages (flame shaped)
Cotton wool spots, swelling of optic disc and exudates
AV change, copper wiring and hemorrhages (flame shaped)
Cotton wool spots, Salus sign and macular star
questions.exp: The grade 3 figure is labelled: cotton wool spots, AV change and hemorrhages (Flame shaped). (Book p164)

questions.q: Which is the most common cause of central retinal artery occlusion according to the book?
opts: Cholesterol emboli from a Hollenhorst plaque
questions.exp: CRAO causes: Atherosclerosis (m/c), emboli (Hollenhorst plaque) and giant cell arteritis. Hypertension is the m/c cause of CRVO (p166). (Book p165)

questions.q: A Hollenhorst plaque consists of cholesterol emboli originating from the bifurcation of the ___.
questions.exp: Emboli: Hollenhorst plaque - cholesterol emboli originating from bifurcation of CCA. (Book p165)

questions.q: All of the following are listed as causes of CRAO in the book EXCEPT:
questions.exp: The listed causes of CRAO are atherosclerosis (m/c), emboli (Hollenhorst plaque) and giant cell arteritis. Hypertension is the m/c cause of CRVO. (Book p165)

questions.q: A patient reports sudden, painless loss of vision in one eye from CRAO. Which type of optic atrophy does the book say follows?
questions.exp: Clinical features of CRAO: sudden, painless loss of vision; optic atrophy (Consecutive). (Book p165)

questions.q: In CRAO, RAPD is also called the ___ pupil.
questions.exp: Clinical features: RAPD or Marcus Gunn pupil. (Book p165)

questions.q: Match the fundus appearance in CRAO with its cause — 1) Pale fundus  2) Cattle tracking fundus  3) Cherry red spot at macula  … A) Segmentation of blood column  B) Retinal edema  C) Collection of fluid in ganglion cell layers except at foveola
questions.exp: Pale fundus d/t retinal edema; cattle tracking fundus d/t segmentation of blood column; cherry red spot at macula d/t collection of fluid in the GCL of retina except at foveola. (Book p165)

questions.q: The fundus photograph placed beside the CRAO clinical features carries the caption '___', with an arrow pointing at the macular spot.
questions.exp: Figure caption: Cherry red spot. ('Tomato ketchup/splash appearance' is the CRVO figure on p166.) (Book p165)

questions.q: A CRAO fundus photograph shows the macula spared, and the fluorescein angiogram shows dye filling one arterial channel. Which vessel do the book's captions name?
opts: Superior temporal branch of the central retinal artery
questions.exp: Captions: 'CRAO with macular cilioretinal artery sparing' and 'Dye filling cilioretinal artery in FFA'. (Book p165)

questions.q: 'Cherry trees never grow tall in sand, mud & grime' is the book's mnemonic for the causes of:
opts: Tomato ketchup appearance of the fundus
questions.exp: Note: Cherry red spots at macula - mnemonic: Cherry trees never grow tall in sand, mud & grime. (Book p165)

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT among the conditions the book lists for cherry red spot at macula?
questions.exp: The list begins CRAO, Trauma-blunt, Niemann Picks disease ... Eales' disease is a separate condition (p168). (Book p165)

questions.q: In the book's cherry red spot list, which gangliosidosis is written on its own line, NOT bracketed with Tay Sachs and Sandhoffs disease?
questions.exp: The list gives Gangliosidosis Type 1 separately; Tay Sachs and Sandhoffs disease are bracketed together as Gangliosidosis Type 2. (Book p165)

questions.q: Tay Sachs disease and Sandhoffs disease are bracketed in the cherry red spot list as Gangliosidosis Type ___.
questions.exp: Tay Sachs disease and Sandhoffs disease are bracketed together as Gangliosidosis Type 2. (Book p165)

questions.q: True or false — 'Any type of Gaucher's disease is listed for cherry red spot at macula.' Choose the correct verdict:
opts: True - the list names Gaucher's disease without specifying a type
False - the book lists Gaucher's disease: Type 1
False - Gaucher's disease is bracketed with Tay Sachs disease as Type 2 gangliosidosis
False - the book lists Gaucher's disease: Type 2 (after metachromatic leukodystrophy)
questions.exp: The list ends with metachromatic leukodystrophy and Gaucher's disease: Type 2. (Book p165)

questions.q: How quickly must treatment be started for CRAO, which the book calls an ocular emergency?
questions.exp: TREATMENT: Ocular emergency: Rx within 4 hrs. (Book p166)

questions.q: After how long does the book say CRAO becomes complete occlusion?
questions.exp: 24-48 hrs: Complete occlusion. (Book p166)

questions.q: What is the purpose of ocular massage in CRAO?
opts: To lower IOP by aspirating aqueous
questions.exp: Ocular massage: Dislodge emboli. (Book p166)

questions.q: For vasodilatation in CRAO, the book lists sublingual ___.
questions.exp: Vasodilatation - sublingual isosorbide nitrate. (Book p166)

questions.q: Carbogen, used for vasodilatation in CRAO, is a mixture of:
questions.exp: Carbogen: 95% O2 + 5% CO2 -> hypercarbia -> raised PCO2 -> lowered pH -> vasodilatation. (Book p166)

questions.q: True or false — 'Carbogen causes vasodilatation through respiratory alkalosis with a raised pH.' Choose the correct verdict:
opts: True - hypercarbia lowers PCO2 and raises pH
False - carbogen acts by lowering PCO2 and lowering pH
True - respiratory alkalosis with raised pH causes the vasodilatation
False - hypercarbia raises PCO2 and lowers pH (respiratory acidosis), which causes vasodilatation
questions.exp: The book's chain: Hypercarbia -> raised PCO2 -> lowered pH -> vasodilatation, labelled respiratory acidosis. (Book p166)

questions.q: To lower IOP in CRAO, the book lists IV mannitol and:
questions.exp: Decrease IOP: IV mannitol and paracentesis (aspiration of aqueous). (Book p166)

questions.q: After massage, vasodilators and IOP lowering, what is the last item in the book's CRAO treatment list?
questions.exp: The CRAO treatment list ends with 'Rx of cause'. (Book p166)

questions.q: What is the most common cause of central retinal vein occlusion per the book?
questions.exp: Central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO): m/c cause: Hypertension. (Book p166)

questions.q: In the non-ischemic stage of CRVO, stasis of blood causes hypoxia and raised vascular permeability, leading to ___ and loss of vision.
questions.exp: Non-ischemic stage: d/t stasis of blood -> hypoxia and raised vascular permeability -> macular edema -> loss of vision. (Book p166)

questions.q: Which is NOT listed as treatment for the non-ischemic stage of CRVO with macular edema?
questions.exp: Non-ischemic Rx: intravitreal triamcinolone, 0.7 mg dexamethasone intravitreal implants and anti VEGF drugs. Panretinal photocoagulation is listed for the ischemic stage's neovascular glaucoma. (Book p166)

questions.q: The dexamethasone intravitreal implant of the Geneva study is given in a dose of:
questions.exp: Rx: 0.7 mg dexamethasone intravitreal implants (Geneva study). (Book p166)

questions.q: The ischemic stage of CRVO arises from severe hypoxia causing damage to the ___.
questions.exp: Ischemic stage: Severe hypoxia -> Capillary endothelium damage. (Book p166)

questions.q: A fundus shows severe flame shaped hemorrhages that give a 'tomato ketchup/splash appearance'. Which stage of CRVO is this in the book?
questions.exp: Ischemic stage clinical features: severe flame shaped hemorrhages; figure caption Tomato ketchup/splash appearance. (Book p166)

questions.q: Rubeosis iridis (neovascularisation of iris) in ischemic CRVO is due to the oxygen demand by the ___.
questions.exp: Rubeosis iridis (Neovascularisation of iris) d/t oxygen demand by posterior segment. (Book p166)

questions.q: In ischemic CRVO, blood leaks into the anterior chamber and blocks the trabecular meshwork. Which glaucoma results, and by what other name is it known?
opts: Neovascular glaucoma, also called 90 day glaucoma
Angle-closure glaucoma, also called 100 day glaucoma
Neovascular glaucoma, also called 100 day glaucoma
Neovascular glaucoma, also called cattle tracking glaucoma
questions.exp: Blood leak into AC -> blocks trabecular meshwork -> neovascular glaucoma: AKA 100 day glaucoma. (Book p166)

questions.q: The '100 day glaucoma' name refers to glaucoma progression of ___ in CRVO.
questions.exp: 100 day glaucoma: Glaucoma progression of 3 months in CRVO. (Book p166)

questions.q: Which treatment does the book give for the neovascular changes of ischemic CRVO?
questions.exp: Rx: Panretinal photocoagulation. (Book p166)

questions.q: What is the most common cause of neovascular glaucoma, per the book's note?
questions.exp: Note: m/c cause of neovascular glaucoma: Diabetic retinopathy. (Book p166)

questions.q: In branched retinal vein occlusion, the ___ part of the central retinal vein is occluded.
questions.exp: BRVO: Superior part of central retinal vein occluded. (Book p167)

questions.q: Match the BRVO feature with its m/c location — 1) m/c site  2) m/c quadrant  … A) Superotemporal  B) AV crossings  C) Optic disc margin  D) Inferonasal
questions.exp: BRVO: m/c site: AV crossings; m/c quadrant: superotemporal. (Book p167)

questions.q: The fundus photograph placed beside the BRVO description is captioned:
questions.exp: Figure caption: BRVO. (Book p167)

questions.q: Per the book, retinopathy of prematurity occurs in infants with an age at birth of:
questions.exp: ROP occurs in: age at birth <= 32 weeks. (Book p167)

questions.q: Per the book, retinopathy of prematurity occurs in infants with a birth weight of:
questions.exp: ROP occurs in: birth weight <= 1750 grams. (Book p167)

questions.q: A baby born at 30 weeks weighing 1500 g is at risk of ROP. When does the book's screening table say to screen?
questions.exp: Age at birth >= 28 wks and birth weight >= 1200 g: screen 4 weeks after birth. (Book p167)

questions.q: A baby born at 26 weeks weighing 1000 g needs ROP screening. According to the table, screening should be done:
questions.exp: Age at birth < 28 wks and birth weight < 1200 g: screen 2-3 weeks after birth. (Book p167)

questions.q: Match the ROP stage with its feature — 1) Stage 1  2) Stage 2  … A) Ridge formation at demarcating line  B) Demarcating line between vascularized retina & peripheral avascular retina  C) Partial RD  D) Total RD
questions.exp: Stage 1: demarcating line between vascularized retina & peripheral avascular retina. Stage 2: ridge formation at demarcating line. (Book p167)

questions.q: Which ROP stage shows extra retinal neovascularization on the ridge moving into the vitreous?
questions.exp: Stage 3: Extra retinal neovascularization on the ridge moving into vitreous. (Book p167)

questions.q: Match the ROP stages with their retinal detachment status — 1) Stage 4  2) Stage 5  … A) Total RD  B) Partial RD  C) Ridge formation  D) Demarcating line
questions.exp: Stage 4: partial retinal detachment (RD). Stage 5: total RD. (Book p167)

questions.q: The two ROP fundus photographs at the foot of the page are captioned:
questions.exp: Figure captions: Stage 2 ROP and Stage 3 ROP. (Book p167)

questions.q: Laser photocoagulation in ROP is indicated in which category, per the ETROP study?
questions.exp: Laser photocoagulation - Indication: Pre-threshold ROP type 1 (ETROP study). (Book p168)

questions.q: One indication for laser in ROP is Zone 1 + ___ + plus disease.
questions.exp: Zone 1 + any stage + plus disease (or). Stage 2/3 with plus disease is the Zone 2 criterion. (Book p168)

questions.q: Which combination is NOT among the book's laser indications for pre-threshold ROP type 1?
questions.exp: Listed indications: Zone 1 + any stage + plus disease; Zone 1 + stage 3; Zone 2 + stage 2/3 + plus disease. (Book p168)

questions.q: Plus disease in ROP means venous tortuosity and dilatation in at least how many quadrants?
questions.exp: Plus disease: Venous tortuosity & dilatation in >= 2 quadrants. (Book p168)

questions.q: An ROP eye has retinal detachment. What additional procedure does the book list?
questions.exp: Pars plana vitrectomy: If RD +. (Book p168)

questions.q: Which set of labels appears on the 'Zones of retina' diagram?
opts: Zones I, II and III, fovea, optic nerve, vortex veins, clock hours, nasal and temporal
Zones I, II and III, macula, optic nerve, ora serrata, clock hours, nasal and temporal
Zones I and II, macula, optic nerve, ora serrata, clock hours, superior and inferior
Zones I, II and III, macula, cilioretinal artery, ora serrata, superior and inferior
questions.exp: The zones of retina figure labels Nasal, Temporal, Clock hours, Zone I, Zone II, Zone III, Macula, Optic Nerve and Ora serrata. (Book p168)

questions.q: Under 'Miscellaneous', which disease does the triangle of Occlusion, Periphlebitis and Neovascularisation of retina leading to recurrent vitreous hemorrhage represent?
questions.exp: Miscellaneous - EALES' DISEASE: Occlusion, Periphlebitis, Neovascularisation of retina -> Recurrent vitreous hemorrhage. (Book p168)

questions.q: Which treatment does the book give for Eales' disease?
questions.exp: Eales' disease Rx: Panretinal photocoagulation. (Book p168)

questions.q: Coats' disease is idiopathic retinal ___.
questions.exp: COATS' DISEASE: Idiopathic retinal telengiectasia. (Book p168)

questions.q: Which pair correctly describes Coats' disease?
questions.exp: Coats' disease: M > F; unilateral. (Book p168)

questions.q: All of the following are clinical features of Coats' disease in the book EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Coats' clinical features: painless loss of vision, strabismus, leukocoria, exudative retinal detachment. Papilledema is a grade 4 hypertensive retinopathy sign. (Book p168)

questions.q: A child with Coats' disease is found to have a retinal detachment. What type of detachment does the book list among its clinical features?
opts: Partial detachment with a ridge at a demarcating line
Detachment of the vitreous with recurrent hemorrhage
questions.exp: Coats' clinical features: exudative retinal detachment. (Book p168)
